subject.title: [Feature]: Skill lifecycle management — auto-optimization on failure + usage-based retirement

question: Should failure-driven skill repair and usage-based skill retirement be built into core Skill Workshop, exposed as plugin/ClawHub lifecycle APIs, or deferred for now?
rationale: The remaining work affects automatic learning from failures, durable metrics, skill visibility, possible deletion, and new config surface, so automation cannot choose the product and ownership boundary safely.

options.title: Design a core/plugin API split
options.body: Specify minimal core state and hooks for failure and usage signals while pushing optional policy and UI behavior to plugin or ClawHub surfaces where possible.

options.title: Keep it core Skill Workshop
options.body: Accept that OpenClaw core owns the metrics, archive state, approval UI, doctor migration, and CLI lifecycle commands for skills.

options.title: Defer lifecycle automation
options.body: Leave current correction-based proposal capture in place and revisit retirement/optimization only after stronger maintainer demand or plugin API gaps are documented.

recommendation.title: Design a core/plugin API split
recommendation.body: Specify minimal core state and hooks for failure and usage signals while pushing optional policy and UI behavior to plugin or ClawHub surfaces where possible.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a roadmap and product-boundary decision, and CONTRIBUTING.md identifies steipete as the project lead.
